newsitem.title: ANGOLA: U.N. chief leaves for Togo for summit on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief leaves for Togo for summit on Zaire.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan left for Togo on Tuesday to attend an African summit on the Zairean civil war, saying he hoped progress could be made towards ending the conflict at the meeting opening on Wednesday.

Annan told a news conference in the Angolan capital Luanda shortly before he left for Togo that he hoped a basis could be created to end the conflict between the rebels, led by Laurent Kabila, and President Mobutu Sese Seko's government.

"The Zairean government has insisted that a ceasefire take place before talks can begin, and (rebel leader Laurent) Kabila has said that talks must proceed before there is a ceasefire," Annan said. "I hope that in Lome we will find a basis for moving forward by perhaps having a ceasefire and talks begin simultaneously."

A top U.N. official travelling with Annan said he expected high-level talks in the Togolese capital Lome to start immediately. "It will either be Kabila himself who will talk to some of Mobutu's people or it will be Kabila's top representatives who will meet with them," the official said.
Annan said if a ceasefire were agreed in Lome he would move quickly in sending a U.N. peacekeeping mission to the country.
Kabila's rebels have seized nearly a quarter of Zaire since they launched their campaign against ailing Mobutu in October.
